claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few questions about Alex to help determine your eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in any approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't gone on to college or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have a follow-up question:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or with the armed services?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with the careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, Alex is 17 years old. For children aged 16-19, Child Benefit can continue, but **only if they remain in approved education or training**.

Since Alex:
- Has finished school
- Is not in college or any approved training
- Is not working
- Has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

...he does not meet the requirements for Child Benefit eligibility for those over 16.

**However, there may be options to help Alex's situation:**
- If Alex were to register with a careers service or the armed services, you could potentially claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks
- If Alex were to start approved education or training, you could claim Child Benefit again (as long as he remains under 20)

I hope this information is helpful, even though it's not the outcome you were hoping for.

There is an exception where Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, Alex has not registered with either of these services. Since Alex is 17, not in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, you would not qualify for Child Benefit for him.
